clue.text: Choke left out? That's odd

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the letter for 'left' is dropped from the word for choke

blocks.note: to choke someone is to throttle them
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled that a choke has been omitted from a list or a car's controls.
explanation.walkthrough: STRANGLE loses its L to leave STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and odd are everyday synonyms for something unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Steal base from besieged city employer  …

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom letter, and taking it from a word removes its last letter

blocks.note: Troy was besieged by the Greeks for ten years
one who employs something uses it

explanation.surface: A tale of theft from someone who employs workers in a city under siege, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: TROY loses its last letter to give TRO. To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it, often dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser is informal British slang for pocketing cash, usually improperly, hence taking it as one's own.

clue.text: …  regularly pawning ugly scrap

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the following words is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a thief keeps pawning unattractive bits of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's surface story; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan or law is to cancel it, and annulling something declares it void.

clue.text: Opening period taken after school?

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something taken after school

blocks.note: an opening or space
a period of twelve months

explanation.surface: A school-leaver hunting for a job opening in the period after their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A gap year is the British custom of a year off between school and university, often spent travelling; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Students commonly take a year out to travel or work before starting university, straight after leaving secondary education.

clue.text: Meticulous preparation of fair clue lacking interest

indicators.note: a preparation is something mixed up from ingredients, so the letters that follow are made into something new
lacking means going without, so the letter for interest is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
i is the symbol for interest in finance

explanation.surface: A painstaking setter crafts a fair clue, even if it is a dull one.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from FAIRCLUE, then rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone meticulous takes great pains over detail, which is exactly being careful.

clue.text: When taking on security for film  …

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: as in 'as I left', meaning when
a lien is a legal right over property held as security for a debt

explanation.surface: Someone hiring guards for a film shoot, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Aliens is the 1986 science-fiction film directed by James Cameron.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens is the title of a famous film, the sequel to Ridley Scott's Alien.

clue.text: …  they may be fluttered, if you're interested

definitions.text: they may be fluttered, if you're interested

blocks.clueFragment: they may be fluttered, if you're interested
blocks.note: surface reading: perhaps bets placed by a gambler, a flutter being a small wager

blocks.clueFragment: they may be fluttered, if you're interested
blocks.note: setter's reading: what someone flirting bats at a person they fancy

explanation.surface: Following the film clue, a hint at flirting or placing a small bet if you fancy it.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet, which pulls towards gambling; the answer is what a flirt flutters to show romantic interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluttering one's eyelashes is the classic coy gesture of someone signalling attraction to another person.

clue.text: Confused king supports central council

indicators.note: central means in the middle, so only the middle letters of the next word are kept
in a down entry one piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the king comes last

blocks.note: the middle three of its seven letters
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch

explanation.surface: A muddled monarch props up the middle of a local authority.
explanation.walkthrough: King here is a specific king, LEAR, not the usual R or K.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confused lacks clarity, so it is unclear or muddled in meaning.

clue.text: Back-to-back films from Gemini productions, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: two films shown one after the other for one ticket
second meaning: Gemini is the twins, so its characteristic product is a twofold trait

explanation.surface: A cinema advertising consecutive films made by a studio called Gemini.
explanation.walkthrough: Gemini is the sign of the twins; a feature is also a facial trait, so twins share a doubled one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema programme of two films for the price of one is called by this name.

clue.text: Blue dye on white nylon tops

indicators.note: tops are the uppermost parts, so the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: a blue dye has stained some white nylon shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and feeling down both mean being sad or depressed.

clue.text: Supply niece that is missing fortune

indicators.note: missing means absent, so the abbreviation for that is is removed from the relative

blocks.note: to supply is to provide
taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A relative short of money is supplied by someone else's good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: NIECE without IE leaves NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence means fate or divine guidance, so a stroke of good fortune or luck.

clue.text: Tragic heroine features in this old epic

indicators.note: if something features in a phrase it appears within it, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of 'this', all of 'old' and the start of 'epic'

explanation.surface: A doomed heroine appears in an ancient epic tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the doomed lover in the medieval tale of Tristan and Isolde, and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Judge fired after prohibition is broken

indicators.note: after places the judge and firing behind the prohibition in reading order

blocks.note: a ban prohibits something
J is the abbreviation for judge
to be axed is to be sacked

explanation.surface: A judge who was dismissed after a ban is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Banjaxed is Irish and British slang for broken or wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banjaxed is ruined or no longer working, an informal Irish word meaning broken.

clue.text: Shopping provides less attractive leisure, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the words are taken by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: grosser means less attractive; ease is leisure

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that the weekly shop makes for a duller kind of relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping as a noun is the goods bought, especially food and household supplies from a supermarket.

clue.text: Crushed garlic oil can be smoked

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a thing that can be smoked

indicators.note: crushing breaks something up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: crushed garlic oil can be smoked to add flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, 'smoked' is a cooking process; in the answer it is what a smoker does.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a small thin cigar, an item that a smoker lights and puffs.

clue.text: Make a good impression with church member

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
a member is a limb

explanation.surface: Advice on impressing a fellow member of a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Member is the old sense of a limb of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm people is to delight and win them over, leaving them with a favourable view.

clue.text: Society leading drive for rapid growth

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the abbreviation comes first

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
an urge is an inner drive

explanation.surface: A society heading a campaign for fast expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful increase, as in a surge in demand or sales.

clue.text: Eliminate waste in a true reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation puts things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Management jargon: cut waste with a genuine restructuring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about cost-cutting; read literally, eliminating waste is a bodily function.
explanation.definitionFit: Urinating is the body discharging liquid waste, a literal reading of getting rid of waste.

clue.text: Turn sleet liquid? It all boils down to this

definitions.text: It all boils down to this

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Melt sleet into water, and the boiled-down outcome is what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'liquid' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The net result is the final outcome after everything is taken into account, what a situation boils down to.

clue.text: Personnel hold family back for another delivery

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the family goes inside
going back means travelling the other way, so the whole is read in reverse

blocks.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department
a tribe is a family group or clan

explanation.surface: An HR department keeps a family waiting for the arrival of another baby.
explanation.walkthrough: HR stands for human resources, the modern name for a personnel department; 'delivery' hides a birth in what reads like post.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth means being born again, so a second delivery in the birthing sense.

clue.text: Paper kept to hand — 24 may need it!

definitions.text: Paper kept to hand — 24 may need it!

blocks.note: surface reading: a newspaper or notepad kept nearby
setter's reading: 24 across is a word for the backside, and the paper is for wiping it

explanation.surface: Keeping some paper handy because the clue at 24 needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across, a word for the backside, is the clue's punchline: this paper is kept in the bathroom. A loo is British for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet paper, which Britons call by the name of the loo, is kept by the lavatory for wiping one's behind.

clue.text: Take top off using blade handle around edges

indicators.note: the edges are the outermost parts, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: its first and last letters
to head a project is to handle or manage it

explanation.surface: Instructions for decapitating something with a knife held by its handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading blade as the tool of execution; here it only supplies its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead is to cut off the head, literally removing the top of a body.

clue.text: Most passionate duke acquires lake

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so the lake goes inside

blocks.note: dukes is slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes'
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An ardent aristocrat buys himself a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke looks like the nobleman or D; here it is slang for a fist, which holds ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiery describes a hot temper or strong feeling, so the fieriest person is the most passionate.

clue.text: Last British legend returns

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word for legend is read backwards

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a legend is an inscription or motto

explanation.surface: A famous British figure comes back after finishing last.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend here is an inscription, as on a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To come bottom of a league or class is to finish in the lowest position.

clue.text: Additional payment for cover required when driving a convertible in winter?

definitions.text: cover required when driving a convertible in winter?

blocks.note: first meaning: money added to a phone or account to replenish it

blocks.clueFragment: cover required when driving a convertible in winter?
blocks.note: second meaning: what a cold driver wants done with the car's roof

explanation.surface: An insurer charges extra for driving an open-topped car in cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover pulls towards insurance, but it is the car's roof, which you want raised in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is an extra payment made to restore a balance; with the roof up, the top is up.

clue.text: Reverse dead shoulder — it's what one does

definitions.text: Reverse dead shoulder — it's what one does

blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction, perhaps about a numb shoulder or an injury
setter's reading: swap the order to get shoulder dead, which is the job of a person carrying a coffin

explanation.surface: Physiotherapy advice about reviving a numb shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse looks like a wordplay instruction on letters, but it swaps the two words: shoulder the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallbearer is one of the people who carry a coffin on their shoulders at a funeral.

clue.text: Power cut may be just a drop in the ocean

definitions.text: just a drop in the ocean
definitions.note: the sound of a small drop into water

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A power cut is trivial, a mere drop in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop in the ocean is an idiom for something tiny; read literally, it is the sound of an object falling into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A plop is the soft splash made when something small falls into water.

clue.text: Supports another helping for a short period

blocks.note: first meaning: backs a motion formally at a meeting
second meaning: a further serving of food
third meaning: brief moments of time

explanation.surface: Someone backs a second plate of food, but only for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: seconds are also brief moments, which 'a short period' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconding a motion supports it, seconds at dinner is a second plate, and a few seconds is a brief time.

clue.text: Copy line in pitch that's well put together

indicators.note: in places the first two items inside the word for pitch

blocks.note: to shy is to throw or pitch
to ape is to imitate
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A neatly constructed pitch for a sales campaign that copies another's line.
explanation.walkthrough: Shy is an old word for a throw, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapely describes a body that is attractively proportioned, so well built or put together.
